sources.title: Climate Risk Profile: Belize
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 profile; mixed historical observations, projections and community assessment findings.
sources.methodology: Desk research and community participation across selected protected-area landscapes.
sources.limitations: Selected CAPA sites; qualitative conflict pathways are unquantified.

sources.title: CORVI: Measuring Multidimensional Climate Risks in Belize City, Belize
sources.temporal_coverage: Assessment published January 2025; includes expert views and data collected through December 2024.
sources.methodology: CORVI combines desk research, 93 expert surveys and 20 interviews.
sources.limitations: Expert-scored Belize City case study; not national or causal.

sources.title: United Nations Belize Common Country Analysis 2021
sources.organization: United Nations Belize, Office of the Resident Coordinator
sources.temporal_coverage: 2021 country analysis; underlying indicators and events span multiple source periods.
sources.methodology: Joint UN analysis; thematic groups scored risks by probability and development impact and consulted stakeholders.
sources.limitations: Dated 2021 analysis; risk ratings and program statements are not measured outcomes.

sources.title: Belize Second National Communication to the Conference of the Parties of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
sources.organization: Government of Belize, Ministry of Natural Resources and the Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: Prepared 2009 and edited through May 2012; includes projections for 2028, 2050 and 2100 and regional water assessments.
sources.methodology: Government sector assessments using climate models and sector studies.
sources.limitations: Old projections and observations; not current measurements.

claims.paraphrase: Assessment covers Belize City, Sarteneja, Dangriga, Hopkins, Seine Bight, Placencia and Riversdale; coastal livelihoods include fishing, processing and tourism, with fishing culturally rooted among Garifuna in Hopkins and Seine Bight.
claims.limitations: Covers seven targeted marine communities, not all coastal settlements.

claims.paraphrase: Among seven assessed marine sites, Placencia ranked most vulnerable and Sarteneja second; Hattieville and Mahogany Heights ranked first and second among 12 terrestrial communities.
claims.limitations: Comparative indices for assessed sites, not a national district ranking.

claims.paraphrase: In the Maya Forest Corridor, the profile links climate-related biodiversity loss and jaguar habitat destruction to more farm/community encounters and residents killing jaguars to protect livestock.
claims.limitations: Qualitative report; no incident count or quantified climate attribution.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The profile links habitat loss to jaguar incursions on farms and residents killing animals to protect livestock.

claims.paraphrase: Women and youth are underrepresented in local climate decisions; Garifuna community members report their input is not fully considered in ecosystem and resource governance.
Low-lying Belize City is exposed to storm-surge, river and rainfall flooding; experts rated extreme-weather impacts the assessment's highest risk.
claims.limitations: Expert-assessed relative risk, not measured annual damage.

claims.paraphrase: Faber's Road Extension is a low-income flood-susceptible area; Krooman Lagoon and London Bridges show expansion threatening coastal ecosystems.
claims.limitations: The examples are qualitative findings from a Belize City assessment.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 5 and 27, Cluster 1 and Economic Risk
claims.paraphrase: CORVI reports some migrants clear mangroves/wetlands for informal settlements, increasing coastal flood vulnerability.
claims.limitations: The report does not quantify the contribution of settlement clearing to flood losses.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It links in-migration, settlement and mangrove/wetland clearing to flood vulnerability.

claims.locator: Printed p. 31, Challenges to Resilience Planning and Action
claims.paraphrase: Belize City's funding dependence and central approval requirements can delay local projects; residents in flood-prone areas often lack electricity, sewerage and clean water.
claims.limitations: Assessment describes institutional conditions at its 2024 data collection period.

claims.paraphrase: The report states that Belize City governments had installed flood-pumping stations and constructed canals to drain floodwaters.
claims.limitations: The assessment reports installations but does not evaluate their flood-risk reduction.

claims.locator: Printed p. 44, Environment and Climate Change Analysis
claims.paraphrase: The CCA reports an IOM-supported government project to build capacity for internal migration and displacement due to climate change; it also notes climate and disaster impacts on livelihoods and coastal systems.
claims.limitations: The CCA reports a program remit, not migration counts or evaluated results.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The CCA identifies internal migration and displacement due to climate change as the program's focus.

claims.paraphrase: The CCA says Mayas and Garinagu are concentrated in Toledo District, where poverty is highest; it records customary Maya land rights and the duty to consult Maya leaders on development.
claims.limitations: Context and poverty findings reflect the 2021 CCA and cited assessments.

claims.paraphrase: The assessment projects lower groundwater recharge in northern Belize, where rice, papaya and sugar use water intensively; central districts face similar pressure, but the water-rich south less.
claims.limitations: Regional projections from an older assessment.

claims.paraphrase: The report says climate-linked runoff decline, pollution and urbanization may degrade water quality, increase competition and produce water conflicts.
claims.scenario: IS92e; GCM/MAGICC with 2.5°C sensitivity; no year stated in passage.
claims.limitations: Projected possibility, not a recorded conflict event.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It says climate-linked scarcity and quality decline may raise competition and cause water conflicts.

claims.paraphrase: Monitoring found saltwater intrusion upstream on the Belize River near the Double Run intake supplying Belize City; the report links it to higher treatment costs and poorer quality.

search_audit.query: Belize subnational climate vulnerability profile Placencia Sarteneja Hattieville Belize City
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the 2025 IISD community assessment with relative marine and terrestrial rankings and the 2025 CORVI Belize City flood profile; rankings cover selected study areas, not all districts.

search_audit.query: Belize climate change conflict water scarcity human-wildlife conflict source report
search_audit.outcome: IISD reports a climate-related habitat-loss/jaguar conflict pathway; the older National Communication projects water competition and possible water conflicts. Neither source documents quantified human violence attributable to climate change.

search_audit.query: Belize migration displacement conflict impacts climate vulnerability reverse link adaptation
search_audit.outcome: CORVI links in-migration and informal settlement ecosystem clearing to increased Belize City flood vulnerability; the CCA reports an IOM-supported climate-mobility response. No inspected source established violence reducing climate adaptation delivery.

search_audit.query: Belize local climate resilience capacity community governance flood adaptation water risks
search_audit.outcome: IISD records community governance inclusion and household adaptation observations; CORVI reports installed flood pumps/canals and municipal bottlenecks; the National Communication documents regional water planning needs.

gaps: No inspected source establishes that climate change caused interpersonal or political violence in Belize; IISD describes human-wildlife conflict and the older National Communication forecasts possible water conflicts, not observed conflict events.
The May 2012 National Communication projections are based on dated models and the reported Belize River saltwater intrusion is not evidence of current conditions.
The IISD rankings cover selected CAPA landscape communities and CORVI covers Belize City; neither provides a comprehensive district-by-district national ranking.

The 2024 First Biennial Transparency Report timed out, FAO's fisheries vulnerability assessment exceeded the browser content limit, and PDC subnational profiles were listed but not accessible as full text; none of these sources supports claims here.
The 2021 CCA reports resource-depletion and competition risks but does not attribute them to climate change; no source inspected established violence as a barrier to adaptation delivery.
